summary: WebDAV never defined what HTTP POST should do on a collection (a folder-like resource), so servers behave differently. This document defines POST on collections as a way to create a new member whose server-chosen name is returned to the client.

plainLanguage.summary: Normally, saving a file in a shared folder means you pick its name. This lets you hand a file to the folder and let the server pick the name instead.

subtitle: A way for a WebDAV server to say where clients can POST new files and let the server pick the name.

tldr.problem: WebDAV never defined what POST does on a collection, so many servers do not support it, and clients often have to invent a unique URL for every new file.
tldr.mechanism: A new protected property, DAV:add-member, tells the client an Add-Member URI that accepts POST to store the body as a new member. The server picks the new URL and returns it in the Location header.
tldr.outcome: Servers can advertise server-assigned member creation without adding a new HTTP method. The scope is deliberately limited to new non-collection resources.

today: RFC 5995 is a Proposed Standard published in September 2010. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why POST on Collections Needs Defining
sections.content:
WebDAV (RFC 4918, Section 9.5) leaves the behavior of POST on a collection unmodified, because HTTP lets servers decide what POST means. The result is that many WebDAV servers do not implement POST for collections at all.

Yet POST suits the job of adding a member where the server controls the new URL. The Atom Publishing Protocol (RFC 5023) already works this way. In contrast, WebDAV-based protocols such as CalDAV (RFC 4791) often make clients pick a unique URL, which is harder for clients and means servers must store a client-supplied name next to an internal identifier such as a UUID or primary key.
sections.plainLanguage: Imagine a mailbox where you must invent a unique name for every letter you drop in. It is easier if you just drop the letter in and the post office labels it for you.

sections.title: The Add-Member URI
sections.content:
The Add-Member URI of a collection is a URI that accepts POST and treats the body as a new internal member of that collection. It MUST be on the same server as the collection (host and port must match).

If creating a resource with PUT in the collection has preconditions, those same preconditions apply to the POST, with the same response body on failure. The new resource's URI comes back in the Location response header.

The Add-Member URI can be the collection's own URI, or a separate one such as /docs/collection/;post. Advertising it implies nothing else about the collection: server-assigned URIs are not necessarily unique over time, since a URI may be assigned again after the earlier resource was removed.
sections.plainLanguage: The server hands you the address of a special drop slot. Anything you push through the slot becomes a new item in the folder, and the server tells you its new address.

sections.title: Discovering the URI with DAV:add-member
sections.content:
DAV:add-member is a protected property on WebDAV collections. It holds the Add-Member URI inside a DAV:href element. A client reads it with PROPFIND.

A PROPFIND/allprop request SHOULD NOT return this property. Servers MUST implement the DAV:supported-live-property-set property from RFC 3253 and report DAV:add-member in it as a supported live property.

In the RFC's example the server answers a PROPFIND on /collection/ with /collection;add-member/, a separate URI minted just for adding content.
sections.plainLanguage: You ask the folder, "where do I put new things?" and it answers with the address of the drop slot.

sections.title: Posting a New Member and the Slug Header
sections.content:
To add a member, the client sends POST to the Add-Member URI with the content. In the RFC's example, a text/plain body of 12 bytes gets a 201 Created response whose Location header gives the new URL.

Clients may send the Slug header field from AtomPub (RFC 5023, Section 9.7) to suggest part of the new URI. Servers are free to ignore it or use any algorithm to build the URI, and should process it as AtomPub defines.
sections.plainLanguage: You can write a name suggestion on a sticky note, but the server may pick a different name anyway.

sections.title: Telling Clients PUT Is Not Allowed
sections.content:
Some collections allow reading as normal WebDAV collections but only accept server-assigned member URIs. They refuse PUT, MKCOL, LOCK, COPY and MOVE that would create a new member at a client-chosen URL.

To explain such failures, the RFC defines the precondition DAV:allow-client-defined-URI. Its element may contain an add-member element pointing to the Add-Member URI. In the example, a PUT to /collection/new.txt fails with 405 Method Not Allowed and a body pointing at /collection;add-member/.

The Add-Member mechanism itself is deliberately restricted to creating new non-collection resources, not collections or the other operations that need a client-specified URL.
sections.plainLanguage: If you try to name your own file and the folder says no, it also tells you where the drop slot is.

sections.title: Access Control and Security
sections.content:
A server MUST reject a POST to an Add-Member URI unless the requesting principal has the DAV:bind privilege on the collection (RFC 3744).

Security considerations of HTTP, WebDAV and XML also apply. Beyond that, deriving the member path from the stored data could expose confidential information, even when only a hash of the content is used.

On servers that do not support this specification, a malicious user could set DAV:add-member as a custom property to trick others into posting to a different URI. Clients can protect themselves by not following DAV:add-member URIs to different servers, and by checking that the property is really a live property.
sections.plainLanguage: Only people allowed to add to the folder can use the slot. Also, check that the slot sign was put there by the folder and not by a trickster.

messages.label: POST /collection;add-member/
messages.note: Sends the content with a Slug header.

messages.label: 201 Created + Location
messages.note: The server-chosen URL of the new member.
